 AFC Bournemouth host Aston Villa in Carabao Cup - Preview

 By

 THE Cherries will bid for a place in the quarter-finals of the League Cup when they host Aston Villa on Wednesday in the last 16 of the competition.
 That would match their best-ever progression in the competition, achieved twice in consecutive seasons in the 2017-18 and 2018-19 campaigns as well as the 2014-15 season.
 But they face a Villa side who, like the Cherries, have started to find their form after a slow start to the season, with both sides boasting perfect records so far in their respective European competitions.
 The Daily Echo previews Wednesday’s game.
 Team news 
 Marco Rose confirmed on Sunday that he would play a rotated side, but he has the benefit of a mostly fit squad to choose from.
 Only Alex Tóth, Alex Scott and Julián Araujo remain out, while Junior Kroupi made his comeback from injury on Sunday at Old Trafford.
 (Image: Richard Crease) 
 The forward will not start as he continues his recovery, but Rose said they will continue to build his minutes up to a full return.
 Villa, meanwhile, are without Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, but Modou Keba Cisse has returned to training and may be involved on Wednesday.
 Head-to-head 
 The two sides do not have a long history of playing each other, with just two meetings in Division Three in the 1971-72 season and two in Division Two in 1987-88.
 The first game between the two after those matches was the only cup meeting between Bournemouth and Villa in the FA Cup in January 2015, when the hosts at Villa Park emerged 2-1 victors.
 (Image: Richard Crease) 
 They have never met in the League Cup before, and it is the visitors to Dean Court who have the better recent record in the head-to-head.
 The sides drew 1-1 in February at the Vitality Stadium, as Rayan cancelled out Morgan Rogers’ first-half opener, after Villa comfortably defeated the Cherries 4-0 in November at Villa Park.
 Form 
 Bournemouth return home after a big win at Manchester United to continue their recent purple patch.
 The 3-0 win at Old Trafford made it 11 goals scored without conceding in the past four games, with 3-0 wins at home against Sturm Graz and AC Milan in the Europa League split by a 2-0 victory over Sunderland in the league, also at home.
 (Image: Richard Crease) 
 That run has got the momentum going at Dean Court, with Rose finally tasting victory in the league after a frustrating start with good performances not rewarded by results.
 Villa also took some time to get going this season after a summer with plenty of change, but they have won three and drawn one of their past four games in the league.
 They have won all three of their Champions League games so far, to leave them second in the league phase of the competition, only behind PSG on goal difference.
 Both sides will be eyeing up a run in the League Cup.
 AFC Bournemouth host Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium on Wednesday, October 28, kick-off at 7.45pm.
